accepted.question_text: Let C₄ denote the 4-cycle, and let f(n; C₄) be the number of labeled graphs on n vertices that do not contain C₄ as a subgraph. Determine the asymptotic growth of f(n; C₄), in particular whether f(n; C₄) = 2^(1/2+o(1)) n^(3/2) as suggested in the source.

evidence.quote: Kleitman and Winston [3] proved f(n; C₄) < 2^cn^(3/2). As far as I know f(n; C₄) = 2^(1/2+o(1))n^(3/2) is still open.

accepted.question_text: Fix c > 0. Among graphs on n vertices with cn² edges in which every edge lies in at least one triangle, let f(n; c) be the largest integer such that some edge is contained in at least f(n; c) triangles. Estimate f(n; c) as sharply as possible from above and below.

evidence.quote: Let G(n; cn²) be a graph on n vertices and cn² edges. Assume that every edge of our graph is contained in at least one triangle. Denote by f(n; c) the largest integer for which at least one edge is contained in at least f(n; c) triangles. Estimate f(n; c) as well as possible both from above and below.

accepted.question_text: Find the smallest integer k > 1 for which there exists an integer n such that gcd(n, n + k) = 1 while gcd(n + i, n + k) > 1 for every integer i with 1 ≤ i < k.

evidence.quote: Find the smallest integer k > 1 and an integer n such that gcd(n, n + k) = 1 and gcd(n + i, n + k) > 1 for each i, 1 ≤ i < k.

accepted.question_text: Let m(4) be the minimum size of a family of 4-element subsets of a set S with the property that every 2-coloring of S makes at least one member of the family monochromatic. Determine m(4), or equivalently improve the known lower and upper bounds on m(4).

evidence.quote: Consider a family of 4-element subsets of a set S that has the property that any 2-coloring of S forces at least one of the 4-sets to be monochromatic. Let m(4) denote the minimal cardinality that such a family may have. ... Can you improve the lower or the upper bound?

accepted.question_text: A graph is called orientably simple if it embeds in the torus T but not in the Klein bottle K. Characterize the orientably simple graphs, without assuming that the characterization must be by excluded minors.

evidence.quote: A graph G that embeds in T but not K we call orientably simple. The problem is to characterize orientably simple graphs, not necessarily by excluded minors.

accepted.question_text: For almost every graph on n vertices, does there exist a collection of cliques such that each vertex belongs to only o(n) cliques and only o(n²) edges remain uncovered? More ambitiously, can one achieve a bound of O(n/log n) cliques per vertex while leaving at most O((n/log n)²) or otherwise comparably negligible uncovered edges, as suggested by the source?

evidence.quote: Does almost every graph have a collection of cliques such that each vertex appears in not too many cliques (<f(n) per vertex) and almost all edges are covered (at most f²(n) uncovered)? ... Can one find cliques with each vertex in o(n) cliques such that o(n²) edges are uncovered? The best possible result would be f(n) = O(n/log n).

accepted.question_text: Let f(n) be the maximum graph distance, under diagonal flips, between two triangulations of a fixed n-gon, where adjacent triangulations differ by replacing one diagonal of a quadrilateral by the other diagonal. Determine f(n), and in particular decide whether the upper bound f(n) ≤ 2n − 10 for n ≥ 8 is optimal.

evidence.quote: Consider triangulations of a fixed n-gon. ... Let f(n) be the maximum distance between two triangulations. It is easy to show f(n) ≤ 2n − 10 (for n ≥ 8), which is conjectured optimal.

accepted.question_text: For coverings and partitions by threshold graphs rather than cliques: first, if a graph family has the property that its nth member can be edge-covered by 2n threshold graphs but requires 3n threshold graphs for an edge-partition, is that gap best possible? Second, among graphs with 2n vertices and n² + 1 edges, what is the correct constant c such that one must contain a threshold subgraph with cn edges?

evidence.quote: I have a family of graphs such that the nth graph can be edge-covered by 2n threshold graphs, but requires 3n threshold graphs to edge-partition it. Is this best possible? ... What is the correct multiple of n?

accepted.question_text: Let c(n) and b(n) denote respectively the numbers of central and bicentral unlabeled n-vertex trees. Determine whether c(n)/b(n) tends to 1 as n tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE: Let c(n) and b(n) be the numbers of central and bicentral unlabeled n-vertex trees, respectively. Then c(n)/b(n) → 1 as n → ∞.

accepted.question_text: For an interval k-coloring of the unit interval, let c(m, k) be the minimum number of cuts needed so that the interval can be partitioned into m disjoint unions of intervals, each containing exactly 1/m of the measure of every color class. Determine whether c(m, k) = (m − 1)k for all m and k; in the source this conjecture is explicitly marked as solved by Alon.

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE: c(m, k) = (m − 1)k. ... REMARK: The conjecture has now been proved by Alon.

accepted.question_text: Given any generating set T of the symmetric group Sₙ, let Γ(Sₙ, T) be the corresponding Cayley graph. Determine whether there exists an absolute constant c such that the diameter of Γ(Sₙ, T) is always less than n^c.

evidence.quote: Prove (or disprove) that there exists a constant c such that for every n and for every set T of generators of the symmetric group Sₙ, the diameter of Γ(Sₙ, T) is less than nᶜ.

accepted.question_text: For a labeling λ of the edges of the complete graph Kₙ by distinct integers 1, 2, …, (n choose 2), let l(λ) be the length of the longest simple path whose edge labels increase along the path, and let f(n) = min_λ l(λ). Determine the asymptotic behavior of f(n), including whether f(n) = o(n) and whether there exists ε > 0 such that f(n) > n^(1/2 + ε).

evidence.quote: Given a labeling λ: E(Kₙ) → {1, 2, …, (n choose 2)} of the edges of Kₙ with distinct integers, denote by l(λ) the length of a longest simple path with increasing labels. Determine f(n) = min_λ l(λ). ... Is f(n) = o(n)? Is f(n) > n^(1/2)+ε for some ε > 0?

accepted.question_text: Find a fast algorithm for determining the diameter of a graph, improving on the matrix-multiplication-based O(n^2.496) upper bound cited in the source and the O(n log n) lower bound mentioned there.

evidence.quote: Find a fast algorithm to determine the diameter of a graph. Using matrix multiplication one can determine the diameter in time O(n^2.496) [1]. On the other hand, the best known lower bound is O(n log n).

accepted.question_text: Is every (2k − 1)-connected graph guaranteed to have a spanning bipartite subgraph that is k-connected?

evidence.quote: Is it true that every (2k − 1)-connected graph has a k-connected spanning bipartite subgraph?
